report.answer_text:
Liquid Glass is Apple’s glass-like software design, unveiled at WWDC on June 9, 2025. It’s not a physical material: buttons, menus, and other interface elements are rendered as translucent layers that subtly bend the image behind them, pick up colors from their surroundings, and shift their highlights as they move. (apple.com)
The design also changes how controls behave. On iPhone, for example, some tab bars shrink as you scroll down to give content more room, then expand when you scroll back up. The glass effect also appears in places like Control Center, the Lock Screen, app icons, and widgets. (apple.com)
Inspired by visionOS, Liquid Glass was introduced across iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, watchOS 26, and tvOS 26. Apple’s aim was to give those platforms a more consistent look while keeping the focus on what you’re viewing. (apple.com)
